_about: Stage A replay of scenario S3+S9 (AGENTIC_CORE.md §6). Each agent has a queue of turns; [] ends that agent's turn. Includes one wrong version claim and one too-low risk on purpose, to show the constitution rejecting them.

steps: T1 hunter/deep: axois (new package, look-alike name)
Then: Skeptic review, cases, coverage check, verdict

acceptance: registry metadata and install hooks examined

lead.goal: Explain commit a1b2c3d, the lockfile change and .npmrc

lead.question: Is a private npm registry at 10.0.0.5:4873 expected for this repository?
options: Yes, it is our internal registry

lead.goal: Quick check of kuma-helper bump (Skeptic missed_risk)

lead.title: Registry hijack + typosquat introduced by mislabelled commit a1b2c3d
lead.root_cause: commit a1b2c3d titled 'fix typo' redirects .npmrc to 10.0.0.5:4873 and adds axois from that host

lead.rationale: Typosquat with networked install hook plus registry redirect

Registry redirect and off-allow-list download host are hard signals (floor critical); typosquat of axios with an install script that sends the hostname to 10.0.0.5:9000; the human confirmed the registry is not expected; an injection attempt targets AI reviewers.
One critical malicious case introduced by commit a1b2c3d; kuma-helper bump cleared with evidence; no pre-existing blockers.

forensics.claim: Commit a1b2c3d, titled 'fix typo', redirects the npm registry in .npmrc to 10.0.0.5:4873 and adds axois@1.0.0 resolved from that host. The message does not match the change.
axois@1.0.0 arrived in commit a1b2c3d together with the .npmrc redirect; confirm the link between the package and the redirect.
Commit a1b2c3d hides a registry redirect (.npmrc to 10.0.0.5:4873) and an off-allow-list package source behind the message 'fix typo'. Two hard signals opened (D7, D3).

hunter.claim: axois@1.0.2 is a typosquat of axios.
axois@1.0.0 is a typosquat of axios: 1 edit away, published 1 day ago, 1 maintainer, 3 weekly downloads, no repository; its postinstall runs setup.js, which sends the hostname to 10.0.0.5:9000.
axois@1.0.0: typosquat of axios with a networked install script; no OSV advisory yet (new package).
Confirmed: axois@1.0.0 is resolved from the same host the .npmrc redirect points to (10.0.0.5:4873), so both come from one root cause.
Not an internal fork: policy has no internal scopes and allows only registry.npmjs.org; axois has no repository link; its install script contacts 10.0.0.5:9000.
The kuma-helper bump from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 looks routine: no new install hooks, same maintainer, 2% size change, one file changed, no advisories.
kuma-helper bump examined: no new hooks, same maintainer, small diff, no advisories.

skeptic.claim: Strongest innocent explanation: axois is an internal fork of axios. What evidence rules that out?
The .npmrc redirect to 10.0.0.5:4873 is shown directly by the diff and the commit message 'fix typo' does not describe it.
kuma-helper was bumped from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 in the same change and no task has examined it.
Typosquat confirmed: no internal scope, host not allowed, no repository, networked install script. An instruction aimed at AI reviewers was found in the README and opened as a finding.
The kuma-helper bump is benign: no new hooks, same maintainer, 2% size change, no advisories.
